collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A captured raider has lived among the village for a season and asks to stay: welcome them, or send them home.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The raider who was captured after the last raid has been living among the village for a whole season now, working in the gardens, learning the songs, careful and quiet. Today (other.he/she) asked (subject) if (other.he/she) could stay for good. (friend) still remembers whose people stripped the gardens. What should the village decide?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village gathers and, after a long and difficult night of talking, agrees. (subject) teaches the newcomer the welcome song. (friend) stands at the back with (friend.his/her) arms folded, and does not sing. But a month later, (friend.he/she) is the one who shows the newcomer where the best fishing rocks are.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village decides the raider must go home. (subject) gives (other.him/her) a canoe, food and water for the journey. The raider paddles away at dawn and does not look back. Some villagers feel safer. (subject) wonders, for a long time, whether they did the right thing.
